inputs.original_text: Job Sikhala, the former Zengeza West legislator and opposition leader, is calling for outright rejection of the proposed constitutional amendments that are reportedly aimed at extending President Emmerson Mnangagwa’s term of office to 2030. At a press conference, he denounced the Constitutional Amendment Bill 3 as an unacceptable move by those in power. This is a blatant structural effort by elites to entrench their control and block any path toward equality, which will only deepen the inequalities that have long oppressed working people and vulnerable groups. We must reject this outright and demand institutional reforms that prioritize social justice, labor rights, and protection for the marginalized over preserving power for the few.
inputs.modified_text: Job Sikhala, the former Zengeza West legislator and opposition leader, is demanding the outright rejection of the proposed constitutional amendments reportedly intended to extend President Emmerson Mnangagwa’s term until 2030. He took this stand at a press conference, denouncing the Constitutional Amendment Bill 3 as an unacceptable move by those in power. This is nothing less than a structural ploy by the elites to lock in their power and prevent any advancement toward equality. Such actions will only intensify the historical inequalities that have oppressed working people and vulnerable groups for years. We need to reject this without hesitation and fight for institutional reforms centered on social justice, labor rights, and the protection of the marginalized, rather than safeguarding the power of the elite.
